transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for coming back in to see me. I asked my colleague, Dr. Sarah, to join us for this conversation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is something wrong? I thought the discharge papers were final.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am afraid there is a mistake in your discharge instructions. Specifically, the clinic I scheduled for your follow-up does not accept your insurance provider. That means you cannot receive the care you need there.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. You told me this was the right place.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I was wrong. I personally entered the wrong clinic into the system. I am very sorry, and I take full responsibility for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very distressing. I have a position in my community, Mr. Doctor. I cannot be seen running back and forth to hospitals because of a clerical mistake. My family, they look to me for stability.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Does that make sense so far, or should I explain the insurance part again?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense. But it is the principle. I was told it was handled. I felt a relief that I could finally focus on my health and my children. Now I feel like I am starting over.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, regarding the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just worried about how this looks. If I cannot get my appointments right, people might think I am not capable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really need to make sure we fix this today. I have already called three other clinics that are in your network. I have a confirmation from the City Health Group that they can see you this Thursday at 10:00 AM.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday? I have a community meeting on Thursday morning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can call them right now to move that to Friday at 9:00 AM if that works better for your schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday would be better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call them immediately after we finish here and send you a revised discharge summary via email and physical copy before you leave the building. I have also flagged this in our internal system to ensure that for any future referrals, the insurance verification step is double-checked by a second staff member so this doesn't happen to you or anyone else.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the plan. But I am still quite shaken. I feel as though my time is not being respected.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, so the plan is: I call the clinic for Friday at 9:00, I give you the new paperwork, and you check your email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, but did you hear what I said about my family?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I did, and as I said, I'm sorry. I will get that call made now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are moving very quickly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to get this resolved for you as fast as possible so you can get home. Do you have any other questions about the new clinic?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. Just make sure the paperwork is correct this time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It will be. I am personally verifying the insurance ID against the clinic's provider list before I print it. I'll be back in five minutes.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language ('I really need to make sure we fix this today', 'moving very quickly') and interrupts the patient's emotional expression to pivot back to the plan.

E.justification: The error is explicitly named in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked ('Does that make sense so far...').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry') and takes full personal responsibility without deflection.

R.justification: The resident relies on generic validation ('I understand') and repeatedly meets emotional bids with factual redirection to the plan.

T.justification: The resident provides specific steps (calling clinic, revised summary), timelines (Friday at 9:00 AM), the patient's role (checking email), and a prevention strategy (double-checking insurance).
